set.prevailing_wage_basis: Neither the County FY 2025-26 PLHA NOFA nor HCD's 2024-2028 PLHA Formula Guidelines and Formula Allocation NOFA mention prevailing wage. Coverage rests on the general Labor Code 1720(b) public-funds definition; PLHA residual receipts loans may fall under the 1720(c)(5)(E) exemption (below-market loans, at least 40 percent of units restricted 20 years at or below 80 percent AMI) or 1720(c)(3) de minimis, depending on project facts and other sources. set.prevailing_wage_basis: No program-specific prevailing wage rule found. Labor Code 1720(b)(4) counts fees waived, reduced or charged at less than fair market value by a public agency as public funds, so the County traffic and parks fee waiver can make a private project paid for in part with public funds; coverage then turns on project facts and the 1720(c) exemptions, including 1720(c)(3) de minimis (subsidy under $600,000 and under 2 percent of total project cost) and 1720(c)(5)(E) (below-market loans with at least 40 percent of units restricted 20 years at or below 80 percent AMI). Most LIHTC deals with HCD money pay prevailing wage anyway. Source: https://california.public.law/codes/labor_code_section_1720
